title: Regular Plural Nouns
keyIdea: A noun names a thing. Singular means one; plural means more than one. Most nouns add -s to make the plural (cat, cats). Nouns that end in s, x, z, sh or ch add -es (fox, foxes; wish, wishes), and you can hear the extra beat. One thing gets no ending, and a word that ends in s, like bus, is not always plural.

kid: A noun is a word for a thing. Cat is a noun. Box is a noun.
One cat. Two cats. When there is more than one, we add s to the end. More than one is called plural.
Some words end in a hiss or a buzz sound, like fox, bus, wish and watch. They get es: foxes, buses, wishes, watches. Say fox-es and clap. You hear one more beat.
Bus ends in s, but it is just one bus. One thing gets no s. One apple. Three apples.
adult: Plural nouns name more than one thing. In England, Year 1 pupils learn the regular plural noun suffixes -s and -es (dog, dogs; wish, wishes), and the spelling rule is taught by sound: if the ending is heard as /s/ or /z/ it is spelt -s; if it is /ɪz/ and adds an extra syllable, it is spelt -es. US Common Core asks kindergarteners to form regular plurals orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (L.K.1c).

The -es words are the ones whose singular ends in a sibilant sound: s, ss, x, z, sh or ch (bus, kiss, box, buzz, dish, bench). Clapping syllables is the easiest check, because the -es always brings its own beat. Irregular plurals (mouse, mice; child, children) and the y to ies change come later, so leave them out for now.

Common mistakes: writing foxs or wishs because the child adds -s to everything; adding -es to words that do not hiss or buzz (penes); adding an ending when there is only one (1 apples); and thinking any word that ends in s is plural, such as bus or grass. Verbs like takes also end in s but are doing words, not plural nouns.

In the lab your child adds animals to a pen and sees the s appear, drags -s or -es onto six words, sorts plurals by one clap or two, finds the real plurals in sentences, and finishes a shop list where one thing gets no ending.

familyTip: Play 'one, two' at tea time: you say 'one cup', your child says 'two cups'. Mix in hissing words like dish, glass and box, and clap together to hear the extra beat in dish-es.

visual.caption: Does each word take -s or -es to mean more than one? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: fill the pens, drag -s or -es, clap the beats, find the plurals and finish the shop list.

practice.hint: Dog ends in g. Does it hiss or buzz at the end?
practice.explain: Dogs. Dog does not end in a hiss or buzz sound, so it just takes -s.

practice.hint: Box ends in x. Say the plural and clap the beats.
practice.explain: {n} boxes. Box ends in x, so we add -es. Box-es has two beats.

practice.prompt: Which word means more than one?
practice.hint: Two of the words end in s but name just one thing.
practice.explain: Cups means more than one cup. Bus and glass end in s, but each is one thing.

practice.hint: Brush ends in sh. What do sh words take?
practice.explain: {n} brushes. Brush ends in sh, so it takes -es, and you hear an extra beat.

pool.hint: Wish ends in sh. Clap it: how many beats?
pool.explain: Wishes. Wish ends in sh, so it takes -es: wish-es, two beats.

pool.hint: Hen ends in n. Does it hiss or buzz?
pool.explain: {n} hens. Hen just takes -s. Hens has one beat.

pool.prompt: There is 1 ... on the plate. Which word fits?
pool.hint: How many are there? One thing needs no ending.
pool.explain: 1 apple. There is only one, so the word has no ending.

pool.hint: Bus already ends in s. What do s words take?
pool.explain: {n} buses. Bus ends in s, so we add -es. Bus-es has two beats.

pool.prompt: Which word has an extra beat when you say it?
pool.hint: Clap each one. Which one needs two claps?
pool.explain: Foxes: fox-es, two claps. Frogs and cats are one clap, so they only take -s.

choices: a word that ends in s
pool.hint: Think of one cat and two cats. Which one is plural?
pool.explain: Plural means more than one. A word can end in s and still be just one thing, like bus.

pool.prompt: In 'Two kids ride the bus', which word is a plural noun?
pool.hint: Find the thing there is more than one of.
pool.explain: Kids is the plural: there are two of them. Bus ends in s but is one bus, and ride is a doing word.
